solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Band of Brothers is on HBO at last, cast discovered

indicators.note: what comes at last is the final item, so only the closing letter of the word is wanted
read as dis-covered, a word with its covering stripped off keeps only its inner letters

blocks.note: the final letter of the TV network's name
the word with its first and last letters removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A TV listings note: the drama series Band of Brothers is showing on HBO, and its cast has finally been revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'A on B' puts A after B, so the pieces join in reverse clue order. 'Band of Brothers' looks like the TV series title, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Oasis was the Manchester rock group led by the feuding Gallagher siblings, Liam and Noel.

clue.text: Before and after

blocks.note: first meaning: formerly, at some earlier time
second meaning: as soon as, as in 'it will be fine when you have arrived'

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like opposites that cannot share an answer; one is an adverb meaning 'formerly' and the other a conjunction meaning 'as soon as'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb sense means formerly or previously; the conjunction sense means as soon as, describing something following another event.

clue.text: On WhatsApp, you’re right to stop one posting submission

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so these letters are pushed into the middle of another word

blocks.note: someone who posts a letter sends it
text-message shorthand for 'you are'
standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone explaining online etiquette: on a messaging app, you are right to stop a person from posting their submission.
explanation.walkthrough: Text-speak spellings like this are a modern crossword device. 'Submission' looks like an entry being posted, but it means giving in.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving in to an opponent or authority is both submission and surrender; the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Some silly verse on a lavatory’s lid

indicators.note: something silly is nonsensical, so the letters are rearranged out of their sensible order
a lid sits on top, and in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A bit of comic poetry printed on top of a toilet seat cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' at the start looks like part of 'some silly verse', but it alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe an indefinite number of things, more than two but not many, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Drive vehicle around Islington’s outskirts — electronic vehicle?

indicators.note: to turn around is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards
the outskirts of a town are its edges, so only the outer letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: to drive something in by force is to ram it
a bus is a vehicle
the first and last letters of the London borough's name
E is the usual abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Someone driving round the edge of Islington, wondering whether their car counts as an electric vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal covers both of the first two words together. Islington is a district of north London. 'Electronic vehicle' looks like an electric car, but only the final 'vehicle?' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine is an underwater craft; the question mark flags that a vessel is an unusual example of something you travel in.

clue.text: Put books in as a refined stocking-filler

indicators.note: to refine something is to process and rework it, so these letters are rearranged
to put one thing in another is to place it inside, with 'in' completing the instruction

blocks.note: the three letters rearranged
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Advice that a few books make a classy present to slip into a Christmas stocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stocking-filler' looks like a small present, but it means the person who fills the stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas is the figure who fills children's Christmas stockings, so the hyphenated phrase describes him literally.

clue.text: Film industry bash coming up, with champagne and whiskey, close to Soho

indicators.note: in a down clue something coming up rises from bottom to top, so its letters read backwards
the close of something is its end, so only the final letter is taken

blocks.note: Bolly is a casual British name for Bollinger champagne
Whiskey is the NATO alphabet word for W
the final letter of the London district
a bash and a do are both informal words for a party

explanation.surface: A movie-business party is coming up near Soho, with champagne and whiskey flowing.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed party word goes at the very end, after BOLLY, W and O. Soho is the London district long home to film companies, which makes 'film industry' feel like part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Bollywood is the nickname for the Hindi-language cinema based in Mumbai, a blend of Bombay and Hollywood.

clue.text: Circus performer with a pair of flyers, one of which is detailed

indicators.note: read as de-tailed, the word has its tail, its last letter, cut off

blocks.note: taken as written
one of the two flying creatures is a crow
the other flying creature is a bat

explanation.surface: A circus performer doing an act with two birds, one of them elaborately decorated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like 'elaborate', but it means losing a tail: the crow becomes CRO, and the bat stays whole.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat performs tumbling, balancing and trapeze feats, a classic act under the big top.

clue.text: Dream Solomon had — Enya ate langoustines for starters

indicators.note: starters come at the beginning of a meal, so each word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: Solomon is the setter, who calls himself I, and 'had' shortens to 'd, so 'Solomon had' is I'D
the opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: The setter describes a dream in which the Irish singer Enya dined on langoustines as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: Solomon is this puzzle's setter, so his name stands for I, the setter speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream job or dream home is the perfect one, so the attributive noun works as an adjective meaning perfect.

clue.text: Is Snoopy broadcast after key Star Trek spinoff?

indicators.note: what is broadcast is heard rather than read, so the sound counts and not the spelling

blocks.note: Enter is a key on a computer keyboard
someone snoopy pries into others' business; the lever-open word sounds the same

explanation.surface: A TV schedule question: is a Snoopy cartoon showing after some major Star Trek offshoot?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snoopy' looks like the Peanuts dog, but it is the adjective 'nosy', so 'is snoopy' becomes 'pries'.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Trek: Enterprise was the prequel television series that ran from 2001 to 2005, named after the starship.

clue.text: Caviar I dropped ruined a new mobile home

indicators.note: something dropped is let go, so the named letter falls out of the word
something ruined is wrecked, so the remaining letters are knocked into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
the letter that is removed
taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that spilling caviar has spoiled their brand-new motorhome.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking I out of CAVIAR leaves CAVAR, which is rearranged before A and N are added.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravan is a towed vehicle fitted out for living in, called a trailer in American English.

clue.text: Greatest coastal resort outside East Timor’s capital

indicators.note: to sit outside something is to surround it, so one piece wraps around another
a capital is a head, so the opening letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: Largs is a seaside town on the Firth of Clyde in Scotland
E is the compass abbreviation for east
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A travel boast about the finest seaside town just beyond the capital of East Timor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East Timor' looks like the country, but East gives E inside the resort and Timor gives only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both superlatives describe the thing of the biggest size or extent, so they are interchangeable synonyms.

clue.text: Bear snarled with fury for four weeks or more

indicators.note: a snarled line is tangled, so these letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An angry bear growling furiously for a month or longer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snarled' plays on a bear's growl, but it means tangled.
explanation.definitionFit: The shortest calendar month has twenty-eight days, exactly four weeks, plus an extra day in leap years.

clue.text: One who makes a bundle filling empty bar with beer

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its contents, leaving only its outer letters
a filling goes inside something, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A publican who makes a fortune by restocking a drained bar with beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes a bundle' sounds like earning a fortune, but it means literally tying a bundle, as a farm machine does with hay.
explanation.definitionFit: A baler is a person or machine that compresses hay, straw or waste into tied bales.

clue.text: One sending letters to the paper?

definitions.text: One sending letters to the paper?

blocks.clueFragment: One sending letters to the paper?
blocks.note: surface reading: a reader who writes letters to a newspaper's editor
setter's reading: a machine that strikes printed characters onto a sheet of paper

explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' means characters of the alphabet, not correspondence, and 'the paper' means a sheet, not a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: This keyboard machine prints characters one at a time by striking an inked ribbon against a page.

clue.text: Sing part of melancholy ode, longingly

indicators.note: a part of something is a piece of it, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Someone sings an excerpt from a sad poem with great yearning.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters bridge three words, ignoring the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: To yodel is to sing with rapid switches between chest voice and falsetto, an Alpine style.

clue.text: Sierra? Porsche overtaking Tesla he’s driven away? Alfa Romeo?

indicators.note: a car that overtakes draws alongside and passes around another, so one piece takes in another
something driven away is sent off, so those letters leave the word

blocks.note: Sierra is the NATO alphabet word for S
taken as written
taken as written: the letters that leave
T is the symbol for the tesla, the SI unit of magnetic flux density
Alfa is the NATO alphabet word for A
Romeo is the NATO alphabet word for R

explanation.surface: A string of car makes, a Ford Sierra, Porsche, Tesla and Alfa Romeo, as if in a race with one car overtaking another.
explanation.walkthrough: Every brand is a decoy: Sierra, Alfa and Romeo are NATO alphabet words, Tesla is the unit symbol T, and Porsche loses HE before taking T in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian marque builds fast, low, agile two-seaters, so it is an example; the question mark signals the example.

clue.text: Those gathering attendants holding hands, slightly apart from one another

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within another
standing a little way apart means the two inserted letters go in separately, with a gap between them

blocks.note: a squire was a knight's attendant
R and L stand for the right and left hands

explanation.surface: Guests at a gathering, attended by servants, holding hands but standing a little distance apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slightly apart from one another' tells you R and L go in separately, with one letter between them, rather than together.
explanation.definitionFit: The rodents famously collect and store nuts for winter, so they are creatures that gather; 'those gathering' is a fanciful description.

clue.text: Work alongside barrel-maker at the back of stable

indicators.note: the back of something is its rear end, so only the closing letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: a cooper makes casks and barrels
taken as written
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone takes a job beside a cask-maker behind a horse stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work alongside' reads like the start of the scene, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To cooperate is to act jointly with others toward a shared goal, which is working together with them.

clue.text: Drum alongside George the Poet

blocks.note: George Ezra is an English pop singer-songwriter
to drum on something is to pound it

explanation.surface: A drummer performing next to George the Poet, a London spoken-word artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George the Poet' looks like one name, the real British performer, but George gives the singer's surname and 'the Poet' defines. The pieces join in reverse clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: The American modernist writer of The Cantos was a major twentieth-century figure in verse.

clue.text: Spice drink raised then drunk by old man

indicators.note: in a down clue something raised is lifted from bottom to top, so its letters read backwards
what is drunk goes inside the drinker, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: kir is a drink of white wine and blackcurrant liqueur
papa is an informal word for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: A spiced drink is lifted in a toast and then knocked back by an elderly man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man' is the familiar term for a father, so PAPA, not an elderly person.
explanation.definitionFit: Paprika is a red powder ground from dried sweet or hot peppers, used to season and colour food.

clue.text: Scrum forward’s bits held by a diff erent player?

definitions.note: read as a plural: more than one scrum forward

definitions.text: bits held by a diff erent player?

blocks.note: first meaning: front-row players in a rugby scrum

blocks.clueFragment: bits held by a diff erent player?
blocks.note: second meaning: objects an actor, a different kind of player, handles on stage

explanation.walkthrough: 'A different player' points away from rugby: an actor is also a player, and handles small stage objects.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the two front-row forwards either side of the hooker share the name with theatrical properties handled by actors.

clue.text: Packages from exotic places are unwrapped

indicators.note: something exotic is strange and unfamiliar, so these letters take on an unusual order
unwrapping removes the outer covering, so only the inner letter of the word stays

blocks.note: taken as written
the inner letter once the outer two are removed

explanation.surface: Deliveries sent from faraway lands are opened on arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unwrapped' fits the packages scene, but it strips the outer letters from 'are'.
explanation.definitionFit: A parcel is an item wrapped up for posting or delivery, which is what a package is.

clue.text: Go over or about mountain-top?

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
a cap is a covering on the top of a peak, as in snowcap

explanation.surface: A climber deciding whether to cross the summit or go round it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go over' sounds like crossing the mountain, but it means summarising again.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise or restate the main points, which is going through them again briefly.

clue.text: Jar of money left inside

indicators.note: something inside is held within, so one piece is placed in the middle of another

blocks.note: cash is money
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A savings jar with coins left in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jar' looks like a container for money, but it is the verb meaning to jolt or conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Colours or opinions that jar are discordant and conflict with each other; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Deliver cracking type of wine specially set aside

indicators.note: to crack something is to break into it, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: red is a type of wine
to serve a writ or a ball is to deliver it

explanation.surface: A sommelier delivering a cracking type of wine kept back for special occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' looks like praise for the wine, but it means breaking into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved table or seat is kept back for a particular person, booked ahead in advance.

clue.text: Hull’s Grand Hotel replacing pillow, finally

indicators.note: what comes finally is at the end, so only the closing letter of the word is used
to replace something is to take its place, so one letter swaps out another

blocks.note: swell is an old-fashioned word for grand or excellent
Hotel is the NATO alphabet word for H
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A hotel in the English city of Hull swaps out its pillows at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull looks like the Yorkshire city, but it is the outer casing; H takes the place of W in SWELL.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer husk of a nut or seed, or the body of a ship, can be called either word.

clue.text: Obscure nonsense cut from the end of promo texts

indicators.note: cutting from the end trims the tail of a word, so the named letters come off its finish

blocks.note: blurbs are short promotional descriptions, as on a book jacket
BS is a slang abbreviation for nonsense

explanation.surface: Meaningless jargon trimmed from the end of marketing copy.
explanation.walkthrough: BS comes off the end of BLURBS. 'Obscure' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb meaning to make unclear.
explanation.definitionFit: To blur something is to make its outline indistinct and hard to see, which is to obscure it.

clue.text: Provider of warm milk one’s beginning to enjoy in the early evening?

indicators.note: a beginning is a start, so only the opening letter of the next word is taken

blocks.note: a teat is the nipple an animal feeds its young from
'one is' is I'M, with one as I and the 's as 'am'
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cosy bedtime picture: warm milk is something to enjoy as the evening begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provider of warm milk' suggests a mug or a cow, but it is the part that supplies it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the late-afternoon meal of tea is eaten around five or six, so the term names that time of day.

clue.text: Face yours truly and shout out loud

indicators.note: spoken out loud, words are judged by sound, so the spelling can change

blocks.note: 'yours truly' is a jokey way of saying 'me', which is I; the organ of sight sounds the same
to bawl is to shout; the round toy sounds the same

explanation.surface: Someone confronts the speaker and yells loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' could be the noun, but it is the verb meaning to confront. Both sound-alikes come from the one indicator at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to stare at them confrontationally, meeting them head on, which is facing them.

clue.text: Drill tries to go through concrete

indicators.note: going through something passes into its middle, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: concrete in the sense of real, actual, not abstract
a judge who tries a case hears it

explanation.surface: A power drill attempting to bore through a concrete wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drill' and 'concrete' make a building-site picture, but drill means practice and concrete means real.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is a practice run of a routine, and a rehearsal is a practice performance before the real thing.

clue.text: Schoolboys wearing trousers use rude words

indicators.note: as a verb, to trouser is to pocket something, so the words hold the letters within them

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: Schoolboys dressed in trousers cursing at one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' looks like clothing, but here it is a verb meaning pockets; 'wearing' is part of the fodder, not the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to curse, using profane or obscene language, which is using rude words.
